items.title: Power Query Corner: Finding and connecting to data in the new experience (Preview)
items.summary: About this series This is the first in a six-part Power Query Corner series exploring the new Power Query experience. Each post takes a closer look at a different part of the experience, including what’s changing, why it matters, and how you can put it to work. Getting data doesn't always begin with a connector name. You might know which database to use, recognize a team-maintained Fabric item, want to return to a source from yesterday, or already have the query logic you need. A connector list is useful once you've decided how to connect. But choosing the right data often comes before that decision. We moved to a module-based approach so Get data can support those different starting points, rather than making every task begin with the same connector picker. The idea is simple: start with what you know, then follow the route that fits the task . Modules organize discovery, reconnection, and authoring around that idea. They don't remove the need to authenticate, select the right objects, inspect a preview, or maintain the query afterward. items.title: Power BI reports support OAP exceptions for semantic models in separate workspaces (Preview)
items.summary: Workspace outbound access protection (OAP) helps you control where data in a Microsoft Fabric workspace can flow. The initial preview for Power BI reports , launched in June, required a report in an OAP-protected workspace to use a semantic model in that same workspace. Customer feedback highlighted that this was too restrictive. With this improvement, a report can now query a semantic model in another workspace provided a workspace administrator explicitly allowed that destination through an OAP exception policy. Apply exception policies to allow report-to-model connections OAP continues to block outbound report-to-model connections by default. When a report opens, Power BI evaluates the report workspace policy before it renders the report in the browser. If the destination workspace is covered by an applicable exception, the report can connect to its semantic model. Otherwise, Power BI blocks the connection, and the report does not open. The report honors the policy that a workspace admin configured for the semantic model destination. items.title: Databricks ADBC connector for Power BI and Microsoft Fabric (Generally Available)
items.summary: This release is part of the broader ODBC-to-ADBC transition for Power Query connectors described in the Transition from ODBC to ADBC drivers in Power BI and Microsoft Fabric documentation. What’s new Existing connections in your semantic models, dataflows, and paginated reports continue to work unchanged — the migration path is currently opt-in per connection, per workspace, or per tenant. Highlights: Improved security - ADBC drivers incorporate security enhancements, such as memory safety and garbage collection. No changes to existing behavior - This transition moves away from the embedded ODBC drivers that ship with Power BI. It does not change behavior for the ODBC connector when you use a separately installed ODBC driver. Efficient large dataset support - ADBC provides a set of standard interfaces for interacting with Arrow data, which is especially efficient at fetching large datasets with minimal overhead and no serialization or copying. Supported authentication - Databricks ADBC supports OAuth (user), OAuth (M2M / Client Credentials), and Microsoft Entra ID.
